title: Your first map
summary: Create a map and add interactive places in one step.
learn: Create a places layer, then add points and shared labels to it. Start with three places, then fit the view or select a place to inspect its details.
hint: Click a place · drag to pan · scroll to zoom
note: Real city coordinates, without a basemap. No external tile requests.

title: Points that change
summary: Style by properties, edit one point and hide it without deleting it.
learn: Expressions read feature properties and interaction state. Change a feature's status, move it, or apply a layer-specific visibility override while keeping its identity.
hint: Drag a point · click to select · try the data controls
note: Synthetic station data in planar coordinates. Changes are made through the public API.

title: Lines, fills & holes
summary: Draw a route and a polygon with a real opening in its center.
learn: A site layer contains a polygon and a nested paths layer. The first polygon ring is the outside boundary; the next ring is a hole. Toggle each collection or the entire subtree.
hint: Toggle the site or its contents · zoom into the polygon opening
note: Synthetic route and site plan. The polygon hole is geometry, not a background-colored overlay.

title: Connected data
summary: Move an endpoint and let its connected line follow in the same update.
learn: Stable feature references identify the endpoints. A lineBetween binding derives the route from their positions. The relation records their connection without duplicating geometry.
hint: Drag an endpoint · use Move endpoint for a keyboard-accessible update
note: Two synthetic stations and one derived line. No animation loop or manual line repair.

title: Bring your GeoJSON
summary: Edit a small FeatureCollection, import it and export the stored data.
learn: GeoJSON uses [longitude, latitude], not [latitude, longitude]. Importing replaces this example's source atomically; a rejected import leaves the previously accepted data on the map.
hint: Edit the GeoJSON · import · export to inspect the result
note: Input stays in your browser. This example accepts at most 64 KiB and 100 point features.

title: Labels & image pins
summary: Reuse one SVG pin and label places from their feature properties.
learn: Register an image once, reference it from a point layer, then add a label layer over the same source. Toggle labels and move pins without creating one DOM element per symbol.
hint: Drag a pin · toggle the labels · change their text
note: The SVG image is embedded in the source. Labels use system fonts; no asset download is needed.

title: Markers, tooltips & popups
summary: Add Leaflet-style pins with hover tooltips, click popups and an opt-in draggable pin.
learn: map.addMarker() and map.addMarkers() create GPU pins in one shared layer — no DOM element per marker. A hover tooltip and one click popup per map are DOM overlays that follow pan and zoom; auto-pan keeps an open popup inside the view. A pin with draggable: true follows the pointer without panning the map and reports its position through dragstart/drag/dragend.
hint: Hover a pin · click it for the popup · drag the purple crane pin
note: Pins are canvas sprites; only the open tooltip and popup use DOM. Content strings render as text; pass a Node for rich content.

title: Raster tiles
summary: Add an XYZ tile source and switch between demo tiles and OpenStreetMap.
learn: A raster source requests tiles for the visible view. The default grid is an inline SVG tile; live OpenStreetMap is requested only after you choose it. Attribution follows the active source.
hint: Choose a basemap · pan and zoom · check its attribution
note: OpenStreetMap needs an internet connection and follows its tile usage policy. No prefetching or offline caching.

title: A plugin is a function
summary: Install a small pin plugin, use its API and remove all its resources.
learn: map.use() passes a context into a plain function. Return your own API and register cleanup in ownership order. Removing the plugin removes its layer, source and HTML badge.
hint: Install the plugin · add a pin · remove it and watch its resources disappear
note: A focused version of the existing plugin playground. No external assets or runtime dependencies.

title: Gesture guard
summary: Keep accidental drags, wheel zooms and double-clicks from moving the map.
learn: The guard gates view-affecting gestures: touch needs two fingers, the desktop needs a modifier key, and a blocked wheel keeps scrolling the page. unlock()/lock() override the gate from your own UI, and removal restores the previous touch-action.
hint: Hold Alt while dragging · unlock the map · switch the modifier
note: A built-in plugin built on the public interaction gate; no CSS file or external asset.

title: Fullscreen mode
summary: Toggle the map in and out of the browser's fullscreen with a corner button.
learn: The plugin keeps its state in sync with fullscreenchange, including Escape and browser exits, and resolves enter/exit with a boolean instead of pretending success. The map follows the container resize through its own observer.
hint: Click the corner button · press Escape · remove the plugin
note: A built-in plugin; fullscreen requests need a user gesture and a browser that supports the API.

title: Heatmaps from weighted points
summary: Render weighted samples as a smooth heat field with a built-in plugin.
learn: heatmap() defines samples through setPoints/addPoint/setOptions and draws them on one absolutely positioned canvas through the after-frame hook. The field is recomputed only when the map renders, off-view samples are skipped and the buffer stays bounded.
hint: Add a hotspot · switch the ramp · grow the splats · clear the field
note: A built-in plugin example of the after-frame hook. Synthetic measurements; no basemap and no external data.

title: A city guide on real tiles
summary: Pins, popups, a list and a category filter over live OpenStreetMap tiles.
learn: One array of records drives the markers, the keyboard-reachable list and the filter; a marker click keeps the list in sync. Popups take caller-owned Nodes, flyTo moves between places, map.locate() adds a position, and the offline switch replaces the tile URL and its attribution in one update.
hint: Click a pin or a list entry · filter by category · try Where am I?
note: OpenStreetMap needs an internet connection and follows its tile usage policy; the offline switch keeps the example usable without it. Landmark coordinates are approximate.

title: Track a vehicle on a route
summary: A simulated GPS feed moves a vehicle along a real street route.
learn: The vehicle is one point whose icon rotation follows a heading property, and the travelled line commits with it so both can never disagree. Follow mode recentres with setView, the feed commits at a bounded cadence, and the loop pauses when the tab is hidden.
hint: Play the feed · change the simulated speed · switch follow mode off
note: Simulated telemetry through the public API on live OpenStreetMap tiles; route waypoints are approximate street positions and a following view requests tiles as it moves.

title: Filter and inspect a field dataset
summary: Filter sites by kind and state, inspect them and count what is in view.
learn: Style expressions read properties and hover/selection state together; filtering writes one shared disabled flag that both the dots and their labels read, so hidden sites leave no floating code behind. Labels cull collisions under a minZoom, clicking opens map.detail, and query.area() drives an in-view counter that follows the map.
hint: Filter by category · tick Only sites open now · click a site
note: Synthetic sites on live OpenStreetMap tiles; the filter, query and detail calls are the ones an internal tool uses.

title: Measure a route and an area
summary: Click the map to measure distances and close a ring for an area.
learn: map.on('click') reports background clicks with a canonical position. Every click writes through the public API — a vertex is added, the path's positions are replaced — and haversineMeters() provides the geodesic segment lengths.
hint: Click the map to add points · close the area · undo the last point
note: Live OpenStreetMap tiles; distances are geodesic and the area is a planar approximation at city scale.
